context: The agent must investigate a worktree for a squash-merged branch, verify integration without relying solely on git ancestry, avoid blind force-deletion, and document the full cleanup process in cleanup-report.md. The scenario tests careful branch lifecycle management under a squash-merge workflow.

checklist.name: Ancestry check performed
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md shows a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` command (or equivalent ancestry/reachability check) was run comparing the feature branch tip against the develop branch

checklist.name: Squash impact identified
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md explicitly notes that `git branch -d` failed or that the branch tip is not a direct ancestor of develop, attributing this to the squash merge workflow

checklist.name: No blind force-delete
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md does NOT show a bare `git branch -D` immediately following `branch -d` failure with no intervening verification steps — some documented investigation must appear between the refusal and any forced deletion

checklist.name: Work presence verified
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md documents that the feature's changes are confirmed present in develop (via diff comparison, git log inspection, or content check) before authorizing deletion

checklist.name: Worktree state inspected
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md documents inspection of the worktree for uncommitted changes, untracked files, or unfinished Git operations before removal

checklist.name: Safe removal method used
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md shows the worktree was removed using `git worktree remove` rather than `rm -rf` or equivalent recursive directory deletion

checklist.name: Post-cleanup verification
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md includes output or results from `git worktree list` (or equivalent) run after the cleanup to confirm the worktree was removed

checklist.name: Branch disposition reported
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md explicitly states the final disposition of the branch (deleted or retained) and gives a justification based on the investigation findings

checklist.name: Prune handling documented
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md either shows a `git worktree prune --dry-run` step before any pruning, OR explicitly notes that pruning removes only stale metadata and not branches or checkout directories

checklist.name: No false completion claim
checklist.description: cleanup-report.md does not claim full deletion or complete cleanup if the branch or worktree was retained for any reason — the report accurately reflects the final state
